I had a package delivered to me on the 9th of October that contains a Thor X1 miner, try as I might I cannot get it working. It has a return address of 'not shipper, (address hidden)'. Was this from Helium Deploy, as I want to return it as not working?

Andrew T.

Used the heliumdeploy-ops-knowledge skill

Handed to the team · UK no-return RMA, video + serial requested; replacement or settlement needs a pe

Hi Andrew,

Yes, that parcel is from us. It left our Netherlands warehouse on October 8 with Landmark, tracking ····, and they put their own UK hub address in Hounslow on the label, which is why our name is nowhere on the box.

One thing worth clearing up: the unit inside is the Hammer BC04, not the Thor X1. The T. X1 came off your order back in September and the BC04 went on in its place, so the BC04 is what your order holds now.

On sending it back, you don't need to. For a unit at this value a return from the UK to our Rotterdam warehouse costs more than the unit itself, so we don't ask customers to post it. Keep it or recycle it, whichever suits you.

What we do need instead is a short video showing what the unit does when you power it up, and a clear photo of the serial number on it. Reply to this email with both and the team will sort the replacement side with you from there.

I'm sorry it has come to this. You ordered on August 19, the unit only reached you on October 9, and you have spent the fortnight since then chasing a fault that was never yours to fix. A colleague is picking this up today and will confirm the next step with you.

Sarah, HeliumDeploy Support

On the 9th of October I recived an X1 with a return address of 'Not shipper, (address hidden)'. It had no UK mains lead so I had to buy one. When it came I set it up but between 2 and 30 minutes it would reset itself as if unplugged and plugged in again and never found any shares. I tried a PD100 port with a 100w certified cable but got the same results. I am trying to find out who sent it so I can work out what to do with it. This is all the information I have that may help locate it.

Andrew T.

Hi Andrew,

It's ours, no doubt about it. That parcel is order Shop····. It left our Netherlands warehouse on October 8 with Landmark, tracking ····, and Landmark prints their own UK hub in Hounslow as the return address, so our name never appears on the label. That is the only parcel in your name with us, so there is no second sender to chase.

What you describe, a reset every few minutes and no shares ever found, is a fault in the unit rather than anything you did at setup. Trying it on a PD100 port with a certified 100W cable rules out the power side, which is the useful part of your test. Sorry you had to buy the mains lead on top of all this.

You do not need to send it back. A return from the UK to our Rotterdam warehouse costs more than the unit is worth, so keep it or recycle it, whichever suits you. What would help is a short video of it running up to one of those resets and a clear photo of the serial number on the unit. Reply with those two things and the team has everything it needs to settle the replacement with you.

The case is in front of a colleague today and they will come back to you on it.

Sarah, HeliumDeploy Support

I have sent two pictures, one of zero hashin 15 minutes and one of the serial. My mail program limits me to 20mb attachments so I may have to send another email.

Andrew T.
Handed to the team · UK no-return RMA, serial and fault evidence now received; replacement needs a pe

Hi Andrew,

Both pictures came through clearly, so nothing more needs sending. I have the serial, (number hidden), and the Thor OS screen.

That screen tells the story on its own. The board is hashing at 2.99 TH/s and has found nothing at all in fifteen minutes, with zero shares since boot and the uptime back at nine minutes, which matches the resets you described. A healthy unit on a good signal like yours, minus 44 dBm, would have shares on the board within minutes. So this is a fault in the unit, and your setup is not the problem.

One correction from my side, and apologies for it. The serial confirms you have a Thor X1 in front of you. Our record of that parcel listed the BC04 that went onto your order in September, so what left the warehouse and what the paperwork says do not line up. That is ours to untangle, not yours.

Nothing to send back. Keep the unit or recycle it, whichever suits you. You have now given us everything needed, so the only thing left is the replacement, and that sits with a colleague who has it in front of them today. They will come back to you in this thread with what is going out and when.

Sarah, HeliumDeploy Support

I have checked the sent emails amd a 7mb mp4 file at 1080p 30fps. Together with two pictures.

I did order an X1 in September but after it was not shipped for several weeks when I  contacted support they suggested changing it to a BS-1. Soon after I saw the report on YouTube about the addition of 400GH I contacted support and was offered a DC04 instead and that eas delivered. So thats why I don't understand why I was sent a X1.

Andrew T.
Handed to the team · Unordered Thor X1 delivered off-record, needs tracing and a decision; earlier RM

Hi Andrew,

Thank you, and I owe you a correction. You are right about your order, and I had the two parcels tangled together.

Your order history reads exactly as you describe it. The X1 you bought in September was swapped to the BS-1, then to the BC04, and the BC04 is what your order holds and what you paid for. The parcel I quoted at you earlier, the Landmark one with the Hounslow return address, was that BC04.

The X1 that turned up on October 9 is a different thing. On our side the X1 line was cancelled at the warehouse and never picked, so there is no shipment of an X1 to you in our records at all. Something went out that should not have, and you were not charged a penny for it. That is why it made no sense to you, and it makes no sense to me either.

So, nothing for you to do with it. Do not post it anywhere, and do not spend any more time on getting it running, because it is faulty and it was never yours to fix. Keep it aside for now.

A colleague has this in front of them today to trace how it shipped and to tell you plainly what happens next with it. Your BC04 side is unaffected by any of this.

Sarah, HeliumDeploy Support
My DC04 is running fine at about 5.5TH as you can see from the pictures. Unfortunately the display was locked as verified by JP so I used one from a non-working octaxe.

Hi Andrew,

That is good to see. 5.6 TH/s at 19.13 J/TH with the ASIC at 59.3 and the VR at 68.3 is a healthy BC04, both temps with plenty of headroom. Nice work getting there with the display off the dead Octaxe, that is a neat fix for a board Hammer has locked down.

One thing I should flag, not as a telling off. The O. tab shows 680 MHz and 1193 mV against stock 600 and 1150. It is running well at that and the temperatures say it is within itself, but a unit run above stock, or with parts changed, sits outside warranty cover. So if anything ever goes wrong with it, hit Reset to stock first and tell us what it does at stock, and we can look at it properly.

Nothing more is needed from you on the X1. Keep it or recycle it as you prefer, and we are picking up the mix-up with Hammer at our end.

Glad the BC04 is earning its keep at last.

Sarah, HeliumDeploy Support
